Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.
Trails are project-scoped. Trail listing requires an explicit --project (--repo only filters within it), or --mine for your trails across projects.

Current repo: gh/llLucidll/VEGA  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

  checkpoint  Inspect and search checkpoints
                read-only except: delete, explain, push
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
                read-only
  session     Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
                read-only except: adopt, attach, resume, stop
  status      Show Entire status
                read-only
  trail       Manage trails across repositories and branches
                read-only: approvals, list, sessions, show, stack, timeline, watch — others write
  why         Show why a line exists
                read-only

Also available (entire agent-help <command> for any of these):
  read-only, safe to run:
    activity · labs · recap · version
  when the task needs them:
    api · dispatch · doctor
  the user's — suggest, don't run:
    agent · auth · clean · cluster · configure · disable · enable
    login · logout · org · plugin · project · repo · service-account

Drill in for exact, currently-installed flags:  entire agent-help <command>  (e.g. entire agent-help trail)

content.text:
Yes—the eye works better than another status badge. I made **VEGA** larger, scaled the eye to match, and kept the glass pill for the three passive states:

- **Monitoring:** green, closed eye.
- **Anomaly detected:** green, open eye.
- **Council investigating:** purple eye with a pupil that glances left, pauses, then glances right. It stays still with reduced motion enabled.
- **Warden invoked:** the pill disappears. A red serpent eye and **VEGA HAS ASSUMED CONTROL** take over the view, with operator approval status still explicit.

The exact [AmazDooM font](https://www.dafont.com/amazdoom.font) is noncommercial, so I used original angular SVG lettering instead.

[Monitoring preview](/tmp/vega-idle-eye.png) · [Warden preview](/tmp/vega-warden-eye.png). All four states passed Chrome checks; lint and build passed.

import type { Point } from './topologyLayout'

const DOT_STEP = 36
const HOVER_RADIUS = 128

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: Point & { strength: number },
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const soft = new Path2D()
  const bright = new Path2D()
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      let influence = 0
      if (reacting && Math.abs(dx) < HOVER_RADIUS && Math.abs(dy) < HOVER_RADIUS) {
        influence = hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - Math.hypot(dx, dy) / HOVER_RADIUS) ** 2
      }
      // Nudge the dots away from the pointer while brightening the nearest ones.
      const px = x + dx * influence * 0.24
      const py = y + dy * influence * 0.24
      const radius = 0.85 + influence * 1.1
      const path = influence > 0.38 ? bright : influence > 0.07 ? soft : base
      path.moveTo(px + radius, py)
      path.arc(px, py, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    }

import type { Point } from './topologyLayout'

const DOT_STEP = 36
const BASE_SIZE = 1.65

export interface TopologyHover extends Point {
  strength: number
  motion: number
}

type StarPath = Pick<Path2D, 'moveTo' | 'quadraticCurveTo' | 'closePath'>

function addStar(path: StarPath, x: number, y: number, size: number) {
  const shoulder = size * 0.14
  path.moveTo(x, y - size)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x + shoulder, y - shoulder, x + size, y)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x + shoulder, y + shoulder, x, y + size)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y + shoulder, x - size, y)
  path.quadraticCurveTo(x - shoulder, y - shoulder, x, y - size)
  path.closePath()
}

export function drawTopologyDots(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  origin: Point,
  zoom: number,
  hover: TopologyHover,
) {
  const step = DOT_STEP * zoom
  const firstX = (origin.x % step) - step
  const firstY = (origin.y % step) - step
  const base = new Path2D()
  const radius = 106 + 48 * hover.motion
  const reacting = hover.strength > 0.01

  for (let y = firstY; y <= height + step; y += step) {
    for (let x = firstX; x <= width + step; x += step) {
      const dx = x - hover.x
      const dy = y - hover.y
      const distance = reacting && Math.abs(dx) < radius && Math.abs(dy) < radius
        ? Math.hypot(dx, dy)
        : radius
      if (distance >= radius) {
        addStar(base, x, y, BASE_SIZE)
        continue
      }

      // Like the portfolio footer, nearby stars scale up and push radially away.
      const influence = hover.strength * (1 - distance / radius) ** 1.5
      const push = (22 + 8 * hover.motion) * influence / Math.max(14, distance)
      const size = BASE_SIZE + (4.3 + hover.motion) * influence
      const clearCenter = 1 - hover.strength * Math.max(0, 1 - distance / 18)
      const opacity = (0.15 + 0.7 * influence) * clearCenter
      // Keep distant stars low contrast; only the center of the field turns white.
      ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(${Math.round(139 + 116 * influence)}, ${Math.round(174 + 81 * influence)}, ${Math.round(205 + 50 * influence)}, ${opacity})`
      ctx.beginPath()
      addStar(ctx, x + dx * push, y + dy * push, size)
      ctx.fill()
    }
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(139, 174, 205, 0.15)'
  ctx.fill(base)
}

import type { VegaDataSource } from './dataSource'
import { LiveStreamSource } from './liveSource'

  return useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE' ? liveSource : mockSource
}

export function switchDataMode(mode: 'SIMULATED' | 'LIVE', force = false) {
  const current = useVegaStore.getState().dataMode
  if (current === mode && !force) return
  activeSource().stop()
  useVegaStore.getState().setDataMode(mode)
  activeSource().start()
}

  if (useVegaStore.getState().dataMode === 'LIVE') {

  }

- Restore a full-width, semi-translucent header with a centered VEGA wordmark and a thin divider above the graph. Keep the animated, state-colored eye inside the circular VEGA-CORE hub.
- Make the topology pannable, with a sparse hover-reactive dotted background and draggable VM cards that keep their connections and do not overlap.
- Keep anomaly injection on the topology; open node details only through an explicit inspection action.
- Add canvas zoom from 50% to 100% with on-screen and keyboard controls, preserving wheel panning, node dragging, and the chosen zoom after inspection.
- Integrate a borderless telemetry readout into the header with rolling ingestion rate, retention TTL, active window, online endpoint count, captured and flagged events, and snapshot status.

Scope: frontend only. Verified with frontend lint, production build, and Chrome interaction checks in simulated mode.

[Desktop preview](/tmp/vega-dashboard-header.png) · [Mobile preview](/tmp/vega-dashboard-header-mobile.png)

Lint, build, and Chrome checks passed. Changes are local.

- Make the topology pannable, with a sparse hover-reactive dotted background and draggable VM cards that keep their connections and do not overlap.
- Keep anomaly injection on the topology; open node details only through an explicit inspection action.
- Add canvas zoom from 50% to 100% with on-screen and keyboard controls, preserving wheel panning, node dragging, and the chosen zoom after inspection.
- Display a right-to-left telemetry ticker beneath the header, with pause and reduced-motion support. It shows rolling ingestion rate, retention TTL, active window, online endpoint count, captured and flagged events, and snapshot status.

Scope: frontend only. Verified with frontend lint, production build, and Chrome interaction checks in simulated mode.

- **Frontend live mode:** Changes to startup, stream reconnection, snapshot handling, Presenter controls, Observer prompts, and node inspection. These span `frontend/src/App.tsx`, `engine/liveSource.ts`, the store, contracts, and several components.
- **VEGA-CORE artwork:** A larger hub, new state colors, and three untracked PNGs under `frontend/src/assets/`. `PanopticonCanvas.tsx` contains both artwork and live-mode changes.
- **Backend:** 16 modified and 16 untracked files covering Redis retention and window processing, telemetry collection, auth and vault work, demo scripts, and tests.

async def test_jev_high_confidence_auto_contains_without_human():
    signal, findings, events = _fixture()
    assessment = _assessment(
        [_verdict("vm-a", "CONTAIN"), _verdict("vm-b", "NO_ACTION")],
        signal_id=signal.signal_id,
    )
    jev = StubJev(
        JevEvaluation(
            available=True,
            action_choice="quarantine_and_revoke",
            confidence=0.94,
            probabilities={
                "quarantine_and_revoke": 0.95,
                "quarantine_host": 0.04,
                "revoke_credentials": 0.01,
                "escalate_human": 0.0,
            },
            credential_compromise=0.96,
            host_compromise=0.93,
            safe_to_automate=0.91,
            model="jev-1.13.0",
        )
    )
    executor = DryRunContainmentExecutor({"vm-a": "auth0|demo"})
    warden = JevWardenService(jev=jev, executor=executor, vm_subjects={"vm-a": "auth0|demo"})

    decision = await warden.evaluate(assessment, signal=signal, findings=findings, events=events)
    assert decision is not None
    assert decision.requires_human_approval is False
    assert decision.approval_status == "approved"
    assert decision.approval_ref and decision.approval_ref.startswith("AUTO-JEV-")
    assert decision.action_type == "quarantine_and_revoke"
    assert decision.target_hosts == ["vm-a"]  # vm-b (NO_ACTION) excluded
    assert jev.last_state is not None
    assert jev.last_state["enrolled_auth0_hosts"] == ["vm-a"]

    runtime = VegaRuntimeState()
    for ev in events:
        runtime.record_event(ev)
    runtime.council_signal = signal
    enforced = await warden.enforce_decision(decision, runtime)
    assert enforced.execution_status == "contained_dry_run"
    assert runtime.threat_mode == "CONTAINED"
    assert next(n for n in runtime.nodes if n.source_id == "vm-a").status == "isolated"
    assert next(n for n in runtime.nodes if n.source_id == "vm-b").status == "healthy"

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe’s flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request’s `model` field selects which one handles it; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Navigate to header: Current modelsCurrent models

|  | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | $42 / $0.042 | $42 / $0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text, images | Text, images |
| Question types | Choice, Score, Noul, Box | Choice, Score, Noul |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

-   **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
-   **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See Context length. To raise both, see Long context.
-   **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It also reads PNG and JPEG [images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images) anywhere in the request. It does not natively accept audio or video (yet). See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state) for the shapes `state` accepts.
-   **Question types:** [Box](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/box) questions need Jev 1.14.

## Navigate to header: Context lengthContext length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

-   **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
-   **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out) for packing many questions into one request, and [Model jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows. To raise both limits, see Long context.

### Navigate to header: Long contextLong context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Navigate to header: Rate limitsRate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization’s current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits). Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors#handling-rate-limits). Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. To request a higher limit, fill out the [rate limit increase request form](https://support.typesafe.ai/forms/rate-limit-increase-request).

## Navigate to header: AliasesAliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

`jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response’s `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version’s ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Navigate to header: Customizing JevCustomizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

-   Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state).
-   Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced).
-   Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery) for training a downstream classical model on Jev’s probabilities.

## Navigate to header: Data handlingData handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## Navigate to header: Listing modelsListing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, each with a description and a release date. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.14.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.

```
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
```

## Findings

* **Official Direct Provider Pricing:** TypeSafe AI publishes direct model rates under its documentation and official model endpoints (`api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`) for its System One decision models (`jev-1.13.0` and `jev-1.14.0`):
  * **Input Cost:** `$42` per billion tokens, or `$0.042` per million tokens (`$0.04` / 1M reported on specific routes).
  * **Output Cost:** Free ($0) because Jev does not generate conversational text or prose. 
  * **Exact Quote (Documentation):** `Price (per Btok / per Mtok), $42 / $0.042` and `"Price: You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens."`

* **Gateways and Third-Party Interfaces:**
  * **OpenRouter / Opper / LLM Gateways:** These services host or pass through TypeSafe AI models (such as `jev-1.13` and `jev-1.14`). Gateways like Opper pass through the base provider rate without token markups while applying their own platform/gateway fees (e.g., 3% on credit purchases or control plane subscription tiers).

    async def _run_multipass(
        self,
        host: str,
        args: list[str],
        *,
        stdin_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        if not _HOST_RE.fullmatch(host):
            raise ValueError(f"Refusing unsafe host identifier: {host!r}")
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "multipass",
            "exec",
            host,
            "--",
            *args,
            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE if stdin_text is not None else asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        try:
            stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(
                proc.communicate(stdin_text.encode() if stdin_text is not None else None),
                timeout=self.command_timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            proc.kill()
            await proc.wait()
            raise TimeoutError(f"multipass exec timed out on {host}") from None
        return (
            proc.returncode or 0,
            stdout_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip(),
            stderr_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip(),
        )

        if host in self.vm_subjects and _AUTH0_SUB_RE.fullmatch(self.vm_subjects[host]):

        rc, out, _ = await self._run_multipass(
            host,
            ["grep", "-oE", r"auth0\|[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", _VAULT_UNIT_PATH],
        )
        if rc == 0 and out:
            sub = out.splitlines()[0].strip()
            if _AUTH0_SUB_RE.fullmatch(sub):

                return sub

In `backend/vega/council/enforcer.py:249`, Warden adds a quarantine chain at the **top of the VM’s outbound firewall**. These are the two key rules:

```bash
iptables -A VEGA_QUARANTINE -j DROP
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -j VEGA_QUARANTINE
```

The chain allows loopback and TCP traffic to the configured telemetry host on ports `8000` and `8001`. It drops DNS and everything else.

There’s **no exception for SSH replies**, so the rule can cut off the same `multipass exec` connection that installed it. That would explain why Multipass timed out even if the quarantine took effect.
what is this for?

It’s Warden’s **network quarantine**. If Warden decides a VM is compromised, the rule blocks it from sending data out or contacting an attacker, while still letting it send telemetry to VEGA so you can monitor it.

That’s separate from credential blocking, which stops the affected user from accessing Vault. The Multipass timeout is an unintended side effect: the quarantine can also block the connection Warden uses to manage the VM.

def _now_ts() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def _audit(actor: str, message: str, status: str = "ok") -> WardenAuditEntry:
    return WardenAuditEntry(

        timestamp=_now_ts(),
        actor=actor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        message=message,
        status=status,  # type: ignore[arg-type]

class ExecutionResult:
    succeeded: bool
    entries: list[WardenAuditEntry]
    isolated_hosts: list[str]

    """Executes real containment on Multipass VMs, local Vault, and Auth0 Management API."""

    dry_run: bool = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        auth0_domain: str,
        auth0_client_id: str,
        auth0_client_secret: str,
        vm_subjects: dict[str, str],
        telemetry_host: str = "10.97.0.1",
        command_timeout: float = 15.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.auth0_domain = auth0_domain.strip()
        self.auth0_client_id = auth0_client_id.strip()
        self.auth0_client_secret = REDACTED
        self.vm_subjects = dict(vm_subjects)
        self.telemetry_host = telemetry_host.strip()
        self.command_timeout = command_timeout
        self._revoked_subjects: set[str] = set()
        self._quarantined_hosts: set[str] = set()

    async def _run_multipass(
        self,
        host: str,
        args: list[str],
        *,
        stdin_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        if not _HOST_RE.fullmatch(host):
            raise ValueError(f"Refusing unsafe host identifier: {host!r}")
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "multipass",
            "exec",
            host,
            "--",
            *args,
            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE if stdin_text is not None else asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        try:
            stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(
                proc.communicate(stdin_text.encode() if stdin_text is not None else None),
                timeout=self.command_timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            proc.kill()
            await proc.wait()
            raise TimeoutError(f"multipass exec timed out on {host}") from None
        return (
            proc.returncode or 0,
            stdout_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip(),
            stderr_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip(),
        )

"""Exercise the quarantine shell script with fake guest commands; never touch a VM."""

import os
import subprocess

import pytest

from vega.council.enforcer import LiveContainmentExecutor


@pytest.fixture
def quarantine_guest(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    executor = LiveContainmentExecutor(
        auth0_domain="", auth0_client_id="", auth0_client_secret="", vm_subjects={},
    )
    log = tmp_path / "firewall.log"
    log.touch()
    guest_env = {"PATH": f"{tmp_path}:{os.defpath}", "FIREWALL_LOG": str(log)}
    for name, stub in {
        "sudo": 'set -eu\n[[ "$1" == -n ]]\nshift\nunset SSH_CONNECTION\nexec "$@"',
        "iptables": 'printf "%s\\n" "$*" >> "$FIREWALL_LOG"\n[[ "$1" != -C ]]',
        "pkill": "exit 1",
    }.items():
        command = tmp_path / name
        command.write_text(f"#!/bin/bash\n{stub}\n")
        command.chmod(0o700)

    async def run_multipass(host, args, *, stdin_text=None):
        assert host == "vm-a"
        result = subprocess.run(
            args, input=stdin_text, text=True, capture_output=True, env=guest_env, timeout=5,
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout.strip(), result.stderr.strip()

    monkeypatch.setattr(executor, "_run_multipass", run_multipass)
    return executor, guest_env, log


async def test_quarantine_keeps_only_reply_traffic_for_multipass_ssh(quarantine_guest):
    executor, guest_env, log = quarantine_guest
    guest_env["SSH_CONNECTION"] = "192.0.2.10 50954 192.0.2.11 22"
    await executor._apply_vm_quarantine("vm-a")
    rules = log.read_text().splitlines()
    ssh_reply = (
        "-A VEGA_QUARANTINE -s 192.0.2.11/32 -d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp --sport 22 "
        "-m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED --ctdir REPLY -j ACCEPT"
    )
    assert [rule for rule in rules if "conntrack" in rule] == [ssh_reply]
    assert rules.index(ssh_reply) < rules.index("-A VEGA_QUARANTINE -j DROP")
    assert rules[-1] == "-I OUTPUT 1 -j VEGA_QUARANTINE"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("connection", [None, "999.0.0.1 50000 192.0.2.11 22", "192.0.2.10 50954 192.0.2.11 0"])
async def test_quarantine_leaves_rules_unchanged_without_valid_management_connection(quarantine_guest, connection):
    executor, guest_env, log = quarantine_guest
    if connection is not None:
        guest_env["SSH_CONNECTION"] = connection
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="quarantine unchanged"):
        await executor._apply_vm_quarantine("vm-a")
    assert log.read_text() == ""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from typing import Any, Protocol, TypeVar

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)


class StructuredReasoner(Protocol):
    mode_name: str

    async def generate(
        self,
        *,
        system_instruction: str,
        prompt: str,
        response_schema: type[T],
    ) -> T: ...


class GeminiStructuredReasoner:
    """Async Gemini API reasoner using google-genai structured JSON outputs."""

    def __init__(self, *, api_key: str, model: str, timeout_seconds: float = 15.0) -> None:
        self.mode_name = f"gemini:{model}"
        self._model = model
        self._timeout_seconds = timeout_seconds
        self._client = genai.Client(api_key=api_key)

    async def generate(
        self,
        *,
        system_instruction: str,
        prompt: str,
        response_schema: type[T],
    ) -> T:
        response = await asyncio.wait_for(
            self._client.aio.models.generate_content(
                model=self._model,
                contents=prompt,
                config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
                    system_instruction=system_instruction,
                    response_mime_type="application/json",
                    response_schema=response_schema,
                    temperature=0.1,
                ),
            ),
            timeout=self._timeout_seconds,
        )
        parsed = getattr(response, "parsed", None)
        if isinstance(parsed, response_schema):
            return parsed
        if isinstance(parsed, dict):
            return response_schema.model_validate(parsed)
        text = getattr(response, "text", None) or "{}"
        return response_schema.model_validate_json(text)

    assert.ok(before.every((mark) => mark.kind === (bars ? 'bar' : 'dot')))
    const gap = largestGap(before, origin)
    if (bars) {
      assert.ok(Math.abs(gap - turn / before.length) < 1e-6)
      for (const { x, y, dx, dy } of before) {
        assert.ok(Math.abs((x - origin.x) * dx + (y - origin.y) * dy) < 1e-6)
        assert.ok(Math.hypot(dx, dy) > 8)
      }
    } else {
      assert.ok(gap > turn / 4)
    }
    assert.ok(Math.abs(largestGap(after, origin) - gap) < 1e-6)
    const shift = bearing(after[0], origin) - bearing(before[0], origin)
    const radians = Math.atan2(Math.sin(shift), Math.cos(shift))
    assert.equal(Math.sign(radians), i % 2 === 0 ? 1 : -1)
    assert.ok(Math.abs(radians) > 0.16 && Math.abs(radians) < 0.3)
    speeds.push(Math.abs(radians).toFixed(5))
  }
  assert.equal(new Set(speeds).size, speeds.length)
})

  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion()
  const closed = state === 'idle'

  return (

      data-eye-state={state}

        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <defs>
            <clipPath id={apertureId}>
              <motion.path
                initial={false}
                animate={{ d: closed ? CLOSED_APERTURE : OPEN_APERTURE }}
                transition={{ duration: reduceMotion ? 0 : closed ? 0.24 : 0.5, ease: 'easeOut' }}

}
